text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyWhat Can We Learn About Happiness From the People Who Study It?Happiness pioneers recently gathered to discuss the good lifeJCBy Jake Currie6:00 PM CDT on October 27, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleFor centuries, scientists have asked how we can live longer, but only relatively recently have they started asking how we can live happier. The field of happiness research first emerged in the 1970s, coalescing from a nebulous constellation of other disciplines. Now that it’s fully formed in its own right, the pioneers of the field recently gathered to reflect on the past half century of happiness research, publishing the results in the Journal of Happiness Studies. Importantly, this wasn’t a rigorous empirical investigation. Instead, it was a kind of summary of a confab of first-in-their field pioneers who dedicated their lives to studying mental well-being, and even applied some of the lessons they learned along the way.
